blocking.claim: "The design was chosen from more than 70 submissions to a public call for proposals, and it took ten years to raise the funds needed to build it. Getting it built at all took even longer: by Xtra Magazine's 2005 account, the memorial took eight years to complete, 'mired from the outset in bureaucratic red tape and a lengthy public process sometimes fuelled by homophobia.'"
blocking.problem: Arithmetic/chronology contradiction. The sentence asserts the total build process took 'even longer' than the ten-year fundraising period, then cites eight years as that total — but eight is not longer than ten. As written, the page states a comparison whose own cited number contradicts it, which will read to most readers as either a typo (ten vs. eight transposed) or as literally claiming an eight-year span exceeds a ten-year span. Neither is true on the page's own facts; a reader is misled about how the memorial's timeline actually adds up.
blocking.evidence: research/sunset-beach-16.json F19: "it took 10 years to raise the funds" (City of Vancouver Public Art Registry). F21: "vancouver's aids memorial took eight years to complete, mired from the outset in bureaucratic red tape and a lengthy public process sometimes fuelled by homophobia" (Xtra Magazine, 2005). The fact sheet does not list these two figures as a flagged 'conflict' (only the panel/name counts are flagged as conflicts) — the page invented the comparative claim, not the sheet.
blocking.fix: Replace with: "The design was chosen from more than 70 submissions to a public call for proposals; the city took ten years to raise the funds needed to build it. By Xtra Magazine's 2005 account, the entire process — from proposal to unveiling — took eight years, 'mired from the outset in bureaucratic red tape and a lengthy public process sometimes fuelled by homophobia.'" This drops the false 'took even longer' comparison and presents the two sourced figures as two separate measures rather than an ordered pair, without inventing any new fact.

advisory.where: showcase.json timeline (1928 entry, "Crystal Pool opens, segregates swimmers")
advisory.claim: "segregation until 1945 (one day a week for Asian and Black swimmers) gives a nearby beach the nickname 'Brown Skin Beach.'"
advisory.problem: The source's own historical language is vaguer than the page's rewording. The sheet's quote says the pool restricted 'oriental and brown-skinned people' to one day a week — a period term that may have covered a broader or different set of groups than the page's modernized 'Asian and Black.' This is a mild specificity-beyond-the-quote issue (category 2), not a claim a reader would be misled by on the substance (segregation happened), so it's advisory rather than blocking.
advisory.evidence: research/sunset-beach-16.json F43, quote: "because of racial segregation at the pool from its beginning in 1928 until 1945, which allowed oriental and brown-skinned people to swim at the pool only one day a week, the nearby indian reserve beach at false creek became informally known as 'brown skin beach'" (Wikipedia: Vancouver Aquatic Centre).
advisory.fix: Optional: soften to the source's own vaguer terms, e.g. "segregation until 1945 (limiting non-white swimmers, per the source's period language, to one day a week) gives a nearby beach the nickname 'Brown Skin Beach.'" No action required if the current paraphrase is considered acceptable modernization.
